units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
And what else can I do with myself here? I can't set to work at anything.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Why can't you?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: In such weather as this? Without a single ray of sunshine the whole day?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Walks up the room.
Oh, not to be able to work--!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Perhaps it was not quite wise of you to come home?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, yes, mother; I had to.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You know I would ten times rather forgo the joy of having you here, than let you--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Stops beside the table.
Now just tell me, mother: does it really make you so very happy to have me home again?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Does it make me happy!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Crumpling up a newspaper.
I should have thought it must be pretty much the same to you whether I was in existence or not.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Have you the heart to say that to your mother, Oswald?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But you've got on very well without me all this time.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes; I have got on without you. That is true.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: A silence.
Twilight slowly begins to fall.
OSWALD paces to and fro across the room.
He has laid his cigar down.
Stops beside MRS. ALVING.
Mother, may I sit on the sofa beside you?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Makes room for him.
Yes, do, my dear boy.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Sits down.
There is something I must tell you, mother.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Anxiously.
Well?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Looks fixedly before him.
For I can't go on hiding it any longer.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Hiding what? What is it?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: As before.
I could never bring myself to write to you about it; and since I've come home--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Seizes him by the arm.
Oswald, what is the matter?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Both yesterday and to-day I have tried to put the thoughts away from me--to cast them off; but it's no use.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Rising.
Now you must tell me everything, Oswald!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Draws her down to the sofa again.
Sit still; and then I will try to tell you.--I complained of fatigue after my journey--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Well? What then?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But it isn't that that is the matter with me; not any ordinary fatigue--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Tries to jump up.
You are not ill, Oswald?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Draws her down again.
Sit still, mother. Do take it quietly. I'm not downright ill, either; not what is commonly called "ill."
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Clasps his hands above his head.
Mother, my mind is broken down--ruined--I shall never be able to work again!
units.name: OSWALD
